transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 44 mins
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Michael Grant (Oakridge CTO), Sara Lopez (Eng Manager), Ethan Park (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Oakridge wants to ship an AI assistant for customer support. They asked about Redwood quickstart, free credits, and time-to-first-token. Discussed hosted API for quick wins, Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private for compliance. Action items to share pricing, security docs, and schedule POC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Michael Grant: Doing good thanks. Michael here. We'll keep it tight we got 45 minutes.
[00:10] Priya Desai: Awesome. Quick agenda — PLG quickstart overview, how to get time-to-first-token, and then talk through infra & security constraints, and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:18] Sara Lopez: Yep that works. We're mainly focused on how fast we can stand up a test and the costs we should expect, and whether we need Dedicated or if hosted is enough.
[00:27] Alex Kim: Great. So high level — Redwood has a self-serve API for text generation and embeddings, you can sign up, claim free credits, and get to first-token in minutes. Most teams start hosted — it's the fastest path. If you need reserved throughput or data isolation later you can move to Dedicated or Private without changing your API calls.
[00:42] Ethan Park: Quick question on the free credits flow — is that tied to a workspace or org, and does it require corporate card? We have strict procurement.
[00:48] Alex Kim: Good question — credits are tied to the account you create; for enterprise buys we can also do credits via a pilot contract. The quickstart itself doesn't need a corporate card, you get a sandbox that lets you hit endpoints.
[00:58] Michael Grant: What's the typical time-to-first-token in your experience? Like from sign-up to a successful API call for us?
[01:04] Priya Desai: From sign-up to first-token you can be five to 15 minutes if you follow the quickstart — we provide SDK snippets, Postman collection, and example prompts. Most friction is around network egress whitelisting in corporate networks, but functionally it's very fast.
[01:21] Sara Lopez: Latency is a big one for us — we need sub-200ms for short support lookups, and average under 300 for multimodal requests. How does hosted latency look?
[01:30] Priya Desai: For short prompts on the hosted stack we often see p50 in the 60–150ms range depending on model & sequence length. If you need stricter SLAs, Dedicated gives predictable tail latency and you can pin to specific hardware. There is a cost tradeoff.
[01:46] Michael Grant: Cost tradeoffs — can you summarize what matters? We do a lot of small queries so token pricing plus batching/caching matters.
[01:53] Alex Kim: Absolutely — per-token cost plus model choice are primary levers. Redwood Optimize helps with batch/caching recommendations and we'll advise on quantization or alternate smaller model variants for many short queries to reduce unit cost. Also prefix caching helps a lot for repeated prompts like templated support questions.
[02:10] Ethan Park: On security — we require SOC 2 type II, SSO via SAML, and KMS integration for keys. And also egress IP whitelisting for our firewall.
[02:19] Priya Desai: We're SOC 2 compliant, support SAML/SSO and RBAC in the console, and we expose KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated workflows. For hosted we provide audit logs and can support egress IP ranges and VPC peering options depending on plan. We'll send our security brief after this call.
[02:36] Sara Lopez: If we needed private deployment for residency — what's the rough timeline for onboarding Private?
[02:42] Alex Kim: Private deployment is more involved — typical on-prem or VPC Private onboarding is 6–12 weeks depending on your infra and compliance needs. Dedicated is usually much faster — we can reserve capacity in a few days to a couple weeks.
[02:55] Michael Grant: For a POC, do you recommend hosted or Dedicated?
[02:58] Priya Desai: For most customers we recommend starting hosted for the quick wins and to validate product-fit. If you hit throughput or residency constraints, we transition to Dedicated for the POC. That way you get time-to-value fast.
[03:12] Michael Grant: Ok that aligns with what we wanted. Our success criteria for POC would be: 1) <250ms p50 for our standard support prompts, 2) cost below our internal threshold per API call, 3) no PII leakage and audit logs available.
[03:25] Alex Kim: Great — that's a solid, measurable set. We'll design the POC to test those three items.
[03:30] Ethan Park: One more infra note — we have egress via a transit gateway and strict outbound rules, so whitelisting and IP ranges are critical.
[03:37] Priya Desai: We'll need your egress IPs and a quick topology diagram — that helps the SE team pre-configure any networking rules.
[03:44] Sara Lopez: About competitors — we looked at Anthropic and Vertex — we're curious about model parity and pricing differences.
[03:50] Alex Kim: Totally; we'll include a short comparison sheet. Redwood focuses on predictable inference economics and runtime optimizations (batching, KV cache, kernel selection) which tends to reduce unit costs. Also our unified API across hosted/dedicated/private avoids rewrite work later.
[04:10] Michael Grant: Are there any known gotchas with the SDKs? Our stack is TypeScript/Go.
[04:15] Priya Desai: We have SDKs for JS/TS, Python, and REST examples. Go customers typically use the REST or community Go client. We'll include those code snippets in the quickstart bundle.
[04:25] Sara Lopez: For the quickstart, what data is logged on hosted? We need to ensure PII isn't retained in the sandbox.
[04:31] Alex Kim: In the hosted sandbox, we have configurable retention; for enterprise customers we can configure zero retention or private deployment. We'll share the data retention policy in the security brief.
[04:42] Michael Grant: Ok can we talk about concrete next steps and timeline? We're trying to kick off a POC next week if possible.
[04:48] Alex Kim: Yes — next steps: I'll send the PLG quickstart guide and a free credits link today; Priya will pull together a POC runbook with tests for latency/cost/retention; we'll schedule a POC kickoff next Tue or Wed — does that work for you?
[04:59] Michael Grant: Tue works for us.
[05:02] Ethan Park: We'll also share our infra diagram and list of firewall IPs by Friday.
[05:06] Priya Desai: Perfect — I'll include example load profiles and the sample prompts we'll use for measurements.
[05:12] Sara Lopez: One small concern: procurement — we may need a short pilot agreement, do you have a template?
[05:18] Alex Kim: Yes, we'll include a pilot contract template and pricing tiers. For larger commitments we do reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated.
[05:25] Michael Grant: Sounds good. Any other questions?
[05:28] Sara Lopez: Not from me.
[05:30] Alex Kim: Cool, thanks everyone. We'll send the docs and set up the kickoff.
[05:35] Michael Grant: Thanks all.

[End of recorded transcript — timestamps are approximate and transcription may contain errors.]
